title: Who Gets to Build the Frontier for AI | Cohere
gist: Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E targeting up to CAD $7 billion, led by Schwarz Group with NVIDIA and the Government of Canada participating, to become a frontier AI company outside the U.S. and China. It rejects 'frontier fatalism', argues the frontier is jagged so domain systems (notably cyber via the AISLE acquisition) can lead, and lays out a 12-month plan including the Aleph Alpha combination, Cohere Cyber for air-gapped environments, and frontier-scale training with allied partners.

insights.claim: Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E round targeting up to CAD $7 billion, led by Schwarz Group with Bell Ventures, Bullhound Capital, Inovia Capital, NVIDIA, Prosperity7 Ventures and the Government of Canada participating.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A German retail conglomerate leading plus direct state participation signals Cohere's capital base is increasingly sovereign and strategic, not purely VC.
insights.quote: Today, Cohere announced the initial close of its Series E funding round targeting up to CAD $7 Billion, led by Schwarz Group
insights.locator: Today, Cohere announced the initial close

insights.claim: Cohere says its Series E is the largest funding round ever raised by a private Canadian company.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Canada is concentrating national AI ambition and capital in a single champion.
insights.quote: Our Series E is the largest funding round ever raised by a private Canadian company
insights.locator: Research and talent are the foundation

insights.claim: Cohere states the funds will be used to build a frontier AI company outside the U.S. and China, spanning frontier models, a secure platform institutions own, and cyber defenses for democracies.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is pivoting its pitch from enterprise-RAG vendor to allied-sovereign frontier lab, raising its capex ambitions and competitive surface.
insights.quote: We will use the funds to build something increasingly essential in AI: a frontier company outside the U.S. and China.
insights.locator: Today, Cohere announced the initial close

themes.theme: Sovereignty and the China open-model surge

insights.claim: More than 70 percent of open-model tokens served through OpenRouter came from Chinese models earlier this year, up from 3 percent fourteen months earlier.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Chinese open-weight models have rapidly captured the open-model market, sharpening Western sovereignty and security concerns that Cohere aims to monetize.
insights.quote: more than 70 percent of the open-model tokens served through OpenRouter came from Chinese models earlier this year – up from 3 percent fourteen months earlier.

insights.claim: Cohere frames today's enterprise choice as cheap Chinese models versus powerful closed models customers cannot fully inspect or control, a gap it intends to fill.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: The positioning targets buyers who want neither Chinese provenance nor U.S. hyperscaler/lab lock-in.
insights.quote: cheap models from China or powerful ones you can’t fully see into or control
insights.locator: Within a few years, every hospital

insights.claim: Cohere argues that access to AI, like past communications, energy and security technologies, can change overnight due to commercial decisions, export controls or geopolitical events, so allied countries need guaranteed access.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Supply-security arguments support government procurement preferences for domestically controllable AI vendors.
insights.quote: Access can change overnight because of commercial decisions, export controls, or geopolitical events, often with few alternatives.
insights.locator: The need for choice and control

insights.claim: Cohere predicts that within a few years every hospital in Bavaria, bank in New York and agency in Ottawa will run a significant part of its operations on AI.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere sees institutional AI dependency as near-term and pervasive, justifying sovereign-control premiums.
insights.quote: Within a few years, every hospital in Bavaria, every bank in New York and every agency in Ottawa will run a significant part of its operations on AI.
insights.locator: Within a few years, every hospital

insights.claim: Cohere labels the consensus that the AI frontier belongs to two countries and a few companies 'frontier fatalism' and calls it a plan for managed decline that leaves countries renting intelligence via API.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: This is a direct counter to the market view that only the largest U.S./Chinese labs will capture frontier value.
insights.quote: Taken to its logical conclusion, frontier fatalism is a plan for managed decline.

insights.claim: Cohere argues there is no single AI frontier but many domain frontiers, citing Harvard Business School's 'jagged technological frontier', and that system design around the model (context, state, verification, evaluation) often determines success.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: If domain systems can beat general models on valuable tasks, smaller-capex labs can compete without winning the general-model race.
insights.quote: In many domains, success depends not only on the model itself, but on the system around it

insights.claim: AISLE frames vulnerability discovery as a production function with two inputs, intelligence per token and tokens per dollar, so efficient models in a well-designed system can explore and validate more findings.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cost-efficiency of inference can substitute for raw model capability in search-heavy domains like security.
insights.quote: The company describes vulnerability discovery as a production function with two inputs: intelligence per token and tokens per dollar.
insights.locator: AISLE, which will soon join us

insights.claim: After curl founder Daniel Stenberg reported in August that Mythos, OpenAI's Codex Security and ZeroPath found nothing further in curl, AISLE's system identified 18 of the 24 vulnerabilities fixed in curl's October release.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A concrete head-to-head anecdote suggests specialized security systems can outperform frontier-lab tools, supporting the AISLE acquisition rationale.
insights.quote: AISLE's system subsequently identified 18 of the 24 vulnerabilities fixed in curl's October release.

insights.claim: Cohere contends Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview and Project Glasswing advances in vulnerability discovery occurred behind closed doors on terms set by one provider, and do not prove cyber-defense leadership will belong to the strongest general model builder.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is positioning against Anthropic's cyber offering on access and control rather than raw capability.
insights.quote: they do not prove that leadership in cyber defense will belong exclusively to whichever company builds the strongest general-purpose model

insights.claim: Project Glasswing extended Anthropic's vulnerability-discovery work to operators of critical infrastructure in more than 15 countries.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: AI-driven cyber defense for critical infrastructure is already a contested, multinational market.
insights.quote: Project Glasswing extended that work to operators of critical infrastructure in more than 15 countries

insights.claim: Cybersecurity provides verifiable ground truth, since vulnerabilities can be reproduced, validated by maintainers and tested against fixes, making it an ideal environment for improving models.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Verifiable domains are prime RL training grounds, so owning a cyber product doubles as a data and training advantage.
insights.quote: Cybersecurity also offers something uniquely valuable for AI development: ground truth.

insights.claim: Cohere argues domain work improves general models because major reasoning gains have come from reinforcement learning in checkable domains (proofs, passing tests, reproducible bugs), and those skills transfer beyond the domain.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A domain-first strategy is pitched as complementary, not a retreat, from general frontier-model competition.
insights.quote: Some of the biggest recent advances in model reasoning have come from reinforcement learning on specific domains where a computer can check the answer
insights.locator: How the frontiers feed each other

insights.claim: Cohere reports public sector customers ask first for strong multilingual analysis and the ability to read images and documents alongside text, the same capabilities banks, telecoms and hospitals need.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Government demand is shaping Cohere's model roadmap toward multilingual, multimodal document capability that also serves enterprise.
insights.quote: Public sector customers usually ask first for strong analysis across many languages and the ability to read images and documents alongside text
insights.locator: Working with customers on real-world tasks

themes.theme: Airbus analogy for an allied challenger

insights.claim: Cohere cites Airbus as precedent: starting from a fragmented European industry, it competed with a differentiated design (the A300 twin-engine widebody) and in 2025 delivered 793 aircraft to Boeing's 600.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere frames itself as a state-backed, patient-capital challenger that can eventually overtake an entrenched incumbent.
insights.quote: In 2025, Airbus delivered 793 aircraft to Boeing's 600.

insights.claim: Cohere argues an apparently settled market can be moved by a serious competitor with patient investment, a differentiated approach and partners willing to build.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Investors are asked to underwrite a multi-year payoff horizon rather than near-term frontier parity.
insights.quote: The lesson is that an apparently settled market can be moved by a serious competitor with patient investment, a differentiated approach, and partners willing to build.
insights.locator: The lesson is that an apparently

insights.claim: Cohere pitches itself as a second option that benefits the United States too, arguing the US frontier should not carry the competition with China alone, analogous to the GE-Safran CFM partnership alongside Airbus-Boeing rivalry.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: The framing is designed to defuse U.S. political opposition to allied sovereign AI and invite American partners.
insights.quote: The US frontier should not have to carry the competition with China alone.
insights.locator: That is the model we have in mind

themes.theme: Canada and Germany public AI investment base

insights.claim: Ottawa has committed more than C$5 billion to AI since 2017, including about C$742 million for the Pan-Canadian strategy, a C$2.4 billion Budget 2024 package with the C$2 billion Sovereign AI Compute Strategy, and at least C$2 billion in the June AI for All strategy.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Sustained Canadian public spending, especially on sovereign compute, is a policy tailwind for Cohere.
insights.quote: Ottawa has committed more than C$5 billion to AI since 2017

insights.claim: With about half of one percent of the world's population, Canada is home to roughly 10 percent of the world's top AI researchers.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Canada's talent density supports the claim that a frontier lab can be built there if capital follows.
insights.quote: With about half of one percent of the world's population, Canada is home to roughly 10 percent of the world's top AI researchers.

insights.claim: Germany has committed €5 billion to its national AI strategy since 2018 and grown Cyber Valley in Tübingen into one of Europe's largest AI research collaborations; Canada and Germany launched a Sovereign Technology Alliance in Munich this year.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: A Canada-Germany axis, reinforced by Schwarz Group and Aleph Alpha, is emerging as Cohere's core sovereign market.
insights.quote: Germany has made a parallel bet, committing €5 billion to its national AI strategy since 2018

themes.theme: Product roadmap: models, North, Cohere Cyber

insights.claim: Cohere argues that if models are swappable, the durable asset is the layer governing an institution's data and workflows, which its model-agnostic North platform aims to be, running in customer clouds, data centers or air-gapped environments.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is hedging model commoditization by seeking value capture in the on-prem agentic platform layer.
insights.quote: If models are swappable, the durable asset is the layer that governs an institution's data and workflows, and that layer should belong to the customer.

insights.claim: Cohere plans to keep investing in frontier models while building smaller, efficient models, offering a portfolio across price points because the cost of useful capability is falling fast.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Falling capability costs favor a portfolio and deployment-flexibility strategy over a single flagship model.
insights.quote: The frontier is jagged, and the cost of useful capability is falling fast.

insights.claim: AISLE, which Cohere plans to acquire and rebrand as Cohere Cyber, identified more than 500 CVEs in its first year and will run on-premises or air-gapped on customer-hosted models.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is buying a proven cyber product to enter defense and critical-infrastructure security budgets.
insights.quote: Through our planned acquisition of AISLE, which identified more than 500 CVEs in its first year, we are building Cohere Cyber

insights.claim: Over the next twelve months Cohere plans to complete its combination with Aleph Alpha and the AISLE acquisition, launch Cohere Cyber for air-gapped and classified environments, release next-generation models and begin frontier-scale training with allied partners.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: These are concrete, trackable milestones; frontier-scale training implies a large step-up in compute spend.
insights.quote: We will complete our combination with Aleph Alpha and acquisition of AISLE, launch Cohere Cyber for air-gapped and classified environments, release the next generation of our models, and begin frontier-scale training with allied partners.

insights.claim: Reliant AI, which joined Cohere earlier this year, extends the North platform into biopharma and healthcare, and Cohere intends to replicate this vertical approach across more industries.
insights.speaker: @cohere
insights.so_what: Cohere is using acquisitions to build vertical products on top of North, signalling an M&A-led growth strategy.
insights.quote: Reliant AI, which joined us earlier this year, extends North’s capabilities into biopharma and healthcare.
